K2 Sports, LLC is an American sporting goods company headquartered in Seattle, Washington 6. Founded in 1962 by brothers Bill and Don Kirschner on Vashon Island, Washington 7. In 1967, Bill Kirschner named the company K2 (for the world's second-largest mountain and for the two Kirschner brothers) 8. K2 snowboards, a subsidiary, was founded in 1987 9. Parent company: Elevate Outdoor Collective (formerly K2 Sports, previously owned by Kohlberg & Company) [5] 10. Manufacturer reputation: K2 Skis & Snowboards continues to be a leading brand in the industry, offering a wide range of equipment for skiers and snowboarders of all levels. Their commitment to innovation, sustainability, and community has made them a trusted and respected name. 11. manufacturing_location_current: China (Guangdong Province) [8] — K2 moved its manufacturing from Vashon Island to Guangdong, China in 2001 12. Manufacturing location (confirmed by review site): K2 snowboards are primarily manufactured in the Guangzhou Province, China. K2 and Ride snowboards are owned and manufactured by the same company (K2 Sports LLC). 13. gender: Unisex [2] — Unisex Designed to fit men and women. 14. NEW to the 2025 K2 snowboard family is the K2 Almanac! Replacing the Party Platter in the range — model first released for 2024/2025 season [10] 15. Model series: ATV Collection [11] — first collection is ATV (last board is Almanac) 16. board_category: All Mountain - Freeride [1] 17. K2 official category listing: Designed to ride the entire resort and score an A+ in the turning category 18. terrain_suitability: Freeride, Big Mountain, Powder, Piste, Freestyle [2] 19. riding_style: Alternative Freeride [12] 20. terrain_suitability: Entire resort — The Almanac excels as a daily driver, carving groomers with precision while floating through powder thanks to Volume Shift design. 21. purpose-built to be your daily driver and a high performance snowboard 22. Design inspiration: takes inspiration from models like the Party Platter and Excavator, and charts it's own course 23. rider_level: Intermediate - Advanced [1][2][3] 24. skill_level_recommendation: Beginner - Expert [12] — *Comment: The Good Ride rates the riding level more broadly than the manufacturer's Intermediate-Advanced designation, noting that even a committed beginner could try this board.* 25. You have a pretty stable, forgiving ride that I think could work for intermediates all the way up to experts, maybe even a committed beginner who wants to get a little weird and try a short wide to start out could go for it too. 26. skill_level_recommendation: Riders who want one versatile board for the entire resort [2][3] 27. shape: Directional [1][2][3] 28. Directional Shape is designed to be ridden with a slightly longer nose than tail to concentrate pop in the tail while providing plenty of float, flow, and control 29. shape: Tapered Directional [12] — *12mm of taper (nose wider than tail)* 30. camber_type: Twin Combination Camber (camber underfoot with raised tip/tail contact points) [1][2] 31. Directional Combination Camber Profile – The best of both worlds. By blending both traditional Camber and Rocker profiles, Combination Camber gives you all the benefits of both; the pop and precision of camber, and the float and predictability of rocker. 32. The K2 Almanac has a mellow camber underfoot, with equal amounts of early rise at the nose and tail. 33. taper: 12mm (nose wider than tail) [12] — *Reviewer states "12mm of taper in the tail versus the nose, which is much less than the 20mm of taper with the excavator"* 34. flex_rating_10: 5/10 (Mid) [1][3] 35. The Almanac flex is for sure on the medium side. A little stiffer in the tail and maybe a touch softer in the nose. 36. flex_direction: Directional — slightly stiffer tail, slightly softer nose [12] 37. width_options: Standard, Volume Shifted [1] 38. Volume Shift™ – Volume is moved from the tips and tails of traditional snowboard shapes and placed underfoot where it can be better controlled. This makes a wider, shorter design that maintains the same float and stability of a traditional board, but increases mobility and maneuverability. 39. Volume shift sizing recommendation: Downsize 4-10 cm from your usual snowboard length [1][2] 40. Volume shift sizing recommendation (DISAGREEMENT, evo/Blauer/Backcountry): Size down 3-5cm from your usual snowboard length [13][10][14] — *Comment: K2 official site says 4-10cm, while several retailers say 3-5cm. The K2 site also specifically recommends "size down ~5cm" in the product text.* 41. When choosing the Almanac, you'll want to size down ~5cm, due to it's wider than average outline 42. Construction: HybridTech (Hybritech™) [1][2] 43. Hybritech™ is the lightest weight, most durable snowboard construction on the market. Removing all excess sidewall material in the tip and tail and adding a 3D capped edge to increase the bond strength of the fiberglass and decrease the swing weight of the board 44. sidewall_material: ABS sidewalls that taper down to sandwich-like construction in tip and tail [12] — You have ABS sidewalls that then taper down almost into a sandwich-like construction, and the tip and tail. 45. core_material: BAP Core (Bamboo, Aspen, Paulownia) [1][2][3] 46. K2 has blended three species of renewable timber to assemble a core that's strong, lightweight, and designed to enhance dampening without the addition of other materials. 47. sustainability_certification: Sustainably sourced/harvested wood [1][2] 48. laminate: Biax Glass with Carbon Backbone [1] 49. laminate: Biax Glass [1][2][3] 50. Biax Glass – Smooth all-purpose performance with a no-frills design. Fibers are woven together at 0° and 90°, creating a more forgiving flex pattern. 51. construction_material_innovation: Carbon Backbone™ [1][2][3] 52. Carbon Backbone™ – Tip to tail cambered carbon insert running down the center of the snowboard adds response and rebound for precise control on approaches and landing heavy tricks, and adding snap to every ollie. 53. construction_material_innovation: Pre-cambered carbon inlay centered between the inserts [2][9] 54. resin: Bio Resin [2] — Bio-Resin is a replacement for traditional petroleum based resin that doesn't affect performance or usability. 55. The ingredients that go into it are sourced as co-products or waste products of other industrial processes and are manufactured employing green chemistry techniques that reduce the carbon footprint of the material by up to 40% 56. base_material: Sintered 4000 [1][2][3] 57. The sintered 4000 base absorbs wax deep into the material for relentless glide and unrivaled durability. 58. The 2x4 hole pattern consists of two rows of holes spaced four centimeters apart, with each hole in the row two centimeters apart. Snowboard bindings are secured to the board using four bolts. 62. Similar boards identified by The Good Ride: Lib Tech Orca, Gnu Gremlin, Salomon Dancehaul, K2 Excavator, Stranda Biru, Telos Backslash 161. Almanac compared to Salomon Dancehaul: If you are actually getting rid of the dancehaul and want something similar but slightly stiffer and damper, then the Almanac would be it. 162. Excavator is the same shape but a bigger step up, better materials stiffer etc. 163. Forum user comparison: Isnt the almanac basically k2's version of the dancehaul? 164. My understanding it's harder charging while the Almanac more playful (like the DH). — referring to the Excavator vs Almanac [24] 165. The Good Ride comparison note (Dancehaul vs Almanac): Both are "favorite boards to ride switch" on the short-wide list; Dancehaul is poppier but less damp [25] 166. Almanac vs K2 Passport (forum): Passport offers better carving, is more burly and locked in [24] 167. Almanac vs K2 Instrument (forum): Instrument is more nimble and flexy, quicker to react to input [24] 168. User seeking Almanac for dampness, ice grip on east coast: Almanac is appealing to me for dampness, ice grip, down sizing and it being unisex. It screams control but less agility compared to the frontier or mind expander twin. Sounds like it'll charge through crud but sacrifice agility. 169. Forum user endorsement: Awesome fun carving board. 170. This is a unique board, as it can work as a short/wide for some and as an almost-normal size for riders with bigger feet who aren't super heavy or tall 171. Hybritech is the most eco-friendly, lightest, and most durable snowboard construction on the market. Removing all excess plastic material in the tip and tail…reducing thousands of pounds of plastic needed during the manufacturing process 173.
